content: 1. Levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate is indicated for use in females of reproductive potential to prevent pregnancy. Tablets should be taken in the order directed on the blister pack, following the manufacturer’s color-coding for sequence. One active tablet is taken orally once daily for 21 days, followed by one ferrous tablet orally once daily on days 22–28. Safety and efficacy in individuals under 18 years of age have not been established. 2. Co-administration of ethinyl estradiol with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir, with or without dasabuvir, is contraindicated due to the risk of significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN) observed in clinical trials. Ethinyl estradiol-containing medications should be discontinued before initiating hepatitis C combination therapy and can be restarted approximately two weeks after completing the regimen. 3. Atazanavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 4. Belzutifan decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to contraceptive failure or increased breakthrough bleeding. Females of reproductive potential should use effective nonhormonal contraception. Based on animal studies, belzutifan may cause fetal harm. 5. Calaspargase pegol may indirectly interact with oral contraceptives, reducing their efficacy. Concomitant use is not recommended. Females of childbearing potential should use a non-oral contraceptive method. 6. Darunavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 7. Elagolix efficacy may be reduced by estrogen-containing contraceptives due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. The effects of progestin-only contraceptives on elagolix efficacy are unknown. Women should use nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for one week after discontinuing elagolix. 8. Encorafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may result in decreased hormonal contraceptive efficacy. Encorafenib can cause fetal harm, and women of childbearing potential should use highly effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after the final dose. 9. Indinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 10. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Lopinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 12. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Patients should use a contraceptive method not affected by CYP450 enzyme induction (e.g., intrauterine system) or add nonhormonal contraception (e.g., condoms) during co-administration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 13. Nelfinavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 14. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. An alternative method of contraception or a backup method should be used during enzyme inducer co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer. 15. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by weak CYP3A4 induction. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception. 16. Pexidartinib increases the risk of hepatotoxicity. Co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents, including levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate, should be avoided. 17. Pretomanid may increase the risk of hepatotoxicity when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Alcohol and hepatotoxic agents should be avoided. 18. Repotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception. 19. Ritonavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 20. Tipranavir may cause significant changes in estrogen plasma levels when co-administered with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced, and the use of a nonhormonal contraceptive is recommended. 21. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by weak CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration should be avoided. If unavoidable, an additional effective nonhormonal contraceptive method should be used during co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 22. Acetaminophen co-administration with levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate may result in unknown interactions. Caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Ascorbic acid increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by decreasing hepatic clearance. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Atorvastatin increases the levels of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting P-glycoprotein transport. Caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Bosentan decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. An alternative method of contraception or a backup method should be used during enzyme inducer co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer. 26. Brigatinib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by inducing CYP3A4. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Women should use effective nonhormonal contraception during treatment and for at least four months after the last dose. 27. Butabarbital decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. An alternative method of contraception or a backup method should be used during enzyme inducer co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer. 28. Carbamazepine decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. An alternative method of contraception or a backup method should be used during enzyme inducer co-administration and for 28 days after discontinuing the enzyme inducer. 29. Cefaclor decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 30. Cefadroxil decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Cefazolin decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. The risk of contraceptive failure is low, but caution and monitoring are advised.
